In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MD simulations of atomic displacement cascading in iron are in good quantitative agreement with experimental measurements of the energy dependence of primary damage production in iron, including the size distributions of point defect clusters formed during cascade decay.
the primary damage production in reactor pressure vessel steels is not uniform through the vessel.

the NRT model is an adequate basis for predicting the through- thickness variation of dpa, and the through-thickness variations of the fraction of interstitials and vacancies in clusters, but that the NRT-based model for the size distribution of in-cascade point defects is too simplistic to accurately predict the through-thickness variation of the size distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MD simulations provide a more accurate description of the through-thickness variation of primary defect production than the NRT d/pa.

the MD results indicate that the NRT model is a reasonable approximation for the average number of surviving point defect clusters in a cascade, but it is not an accurate description of the size distribution.
the spectrum-averaging of primary defect production is a useful technique for obtaining the depth dependence of the primary defect production cross sections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences in the primary damage production rates for interstitial and vacancy clusters in iron.
the size distribution of point defects clusters formed during the cooling of a displacement cascade in iron exhibits a strong energy dependence.
the NRT dPA is not an adequate metric to describe primary radiation damage in reactor pressure vessels.
